Rashi on Ketubot 26b:1:1.english: And we elevated him - For in the case of a rumor, one [witness] is believed.

Rashi on Ketubot 26b:1:2.hebrew: ודכולי עלמא - בין לר' אלעזר בין לר"ש:
Rashi on Ketubot 26b:1:2.english: And everyone [agrees] - Both according to Rabbi Elazar and according to Rabban Shimon [ben Gamliel].

Rashi on Ketubot 26b:1:3.english: Join together - Two witnesses who testify one not in the presence of the other, [as] in other [cases of] testimony.

Rashi on Ketubot 26b:2:1.hebrew: דחיישינן לזילותא דבי דינא - שהורידוהו שני פעמים, ועכשיו יעלוהו ויבטלו דבריהם. והיינו דקאמר ר' אלעזר, דמאחר שהורדנוהו ע"פ העוררין, אין מעלין ע"פ עד זה השני, אע"פ שיש לצרפו עם האחר:
Rashi on Ketubot 26b:2:1.english: That we are concerned about contempt for the court - For they downgraded him twice, and now they would elevate him and nullify their [own] words. And that is what Rabbi Elazar said, that since we downgraded him on the basis of the challengers, we do not elevate [him] on the basis of this second witness, even though he can be combined with the other [witness].

Rashi on Ketubot 26b:2:2.hebrew: ואנן מסקינן ליה - ואי קשיא: תרי ותרי נינהו? אוקי תרי לבהדי תרי, ואוקמינן אחזקיה קמייתא, דאסקיניה ע"פ עד הראשון שהוא נאמן, דהא אכתי אין עוררין, דקול לאו עוררין הוא:
Rashi on Ketubot 26b:2:2.english: And we elevate him - And if you ask: They are two [witnesses] against two [witnesses]! Set the two against the two, and we establish him upon his original presumptive status, for we elevated him on the basis of the first witness, who is believed, since there are still no challengers, as a rumor is not [considered] challengers.

Rashi on Ketubot 26b:3:1.english: Even two - [if they] come together as well on the second occasion, according to Rabbi Elazar we do not elevate him.

Rashi on Ketubot 26b:4:1.hebrew: עד שיראו שניהם כאחד - את העדות, לאפוקי אחד אומר "בפני הלווהו", ואחד אומר "בפני הודה לו עליו":
Rashi on Ketubot 26b:4:1.english: Until the two of them see as one - [That is, see] the testimony [together], to exclude [a case where] one says, "In my presence he lent [to] him," and one says, "In my presence he admitted to him regarding it."

Rashi on Ketubot 26b:4:2.hebrew: ואין עדותן מתקיימת - להתקבל בב"ד, ואפי' ראו שניהן כאחד. ופלוגתא אחריתי היא, ולאו ר' יהושע בן קרחה קאמר לה. ורבי אלעזר ורבן שמעון בפלוגתא דרבי נתן ורבנן פליגי:
Rashi on Ketubot 26b:4:2.english: And their testimony is not validated - To be accepted in court, even if both of them saw [it] as one. And it is a separate dispute, and it is not Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korḥa who said it; and Rabbi Elazar and Rabban Shimon disagree in the dispute of Rabbi Natan and the Rabbis.

Rashi on Ketubot 26b:6:1.hebrew: ע"י ממון מותרת לבעלה - דמרתתי להפסיד ממונן, ואינן מפקירין אותה:
Rashi on Ketubot 26b:6:1.english: Due to money, she is permitted to her husband - Because they are afraid of losing their money, and [therefore] they do not abandon her [to violation].

Rashi on Ketubot 26b:6:2.hebrew: ע"י נפשות - שהיתה נידונת למות:
Rashi on Ketubot 26b:6:2.english: Due to capital [charges] - [Meaning] that she was sentenced to death.

Rashi on Ketubot 26b:6:3.hebrew: אסורה לבעלה - דהואיל ונוהגין בה הפקר, חוששין שמא נתרצתה באחד מהן:
Rashi on Ketubot 26b:6:3.english: She is forbidden to her husband - For since they treat her licentiously, we are concerned lest she consented to one of them.

Rashi on Ketubot 26b:7:1.hebrew: לא שנו - דע"י ממון מותרת לבעלה:
Rashi on Ketubot 26b:7:1.english: They did not teach [this] - [namely,] that [when imprisoned] due to a monetary [matter] she is permitted to her husband.

Rashi on Ketubot 26b:7:2.english: Except where the hand of Israel is dominant over the idolaters - and they are afraid to act unlawfully, lest they lose their money.

Rashi on Ketubot 26b:8:1.english: That she was taken as collateral - She was taken as a pledge.

Rashi on Ketubot 26b:8:2.english: And her witnesses - Those who testified that she was taken as collateral.

Rashi on Ketubot 26b:9:1.hebrew: והא אשקלון - דארץ פלשתים היא, ועוד כבר גלו ישראל:
Rashi on Ketubot 26b:9:1.english: But Ashkelon - For it is the land of the Philistines, and furthermore, Israel had already gone into exile.

Tosafot on Ketubot 26b:1:1.hebrew: ואסקיניה - וא"ת: ולמאן דחייש לזילותא דבי דינא, היכי אסקוהו, כיון דאחתיניה מחמת הקול? וליכא למימר דליכא זילותא דבי דינא אלא היכא שהורידוהו שתי פעמים, כדמוכח בחזקת הבתים (ב"ב דף לב.)! וי"ל: דליכא זילותא דבי דינא אלא היכא שהורידוהו ע"י עדות, אבל בהורדה שע"י הקול ליכא זילותא דב"ד. ואע"ג דאמרינן (גיטין דף פא.) גבי גרושה לכהן דלא מבטלים קלא — היינו משום דאית ליה תקנתא; אבל הכא, דאי לא מסקינן ליה לעולם פסול, מבטלין. אי נמי: בתרומה דרבנן הקילו:
Tosafot on Ketubot 26b:1:1.english: And we elevated him - And if you will say: According to the one who is concerned about contempt for the court, how did they elevate him, since they had [already] downgraded him on account of the rumor? And one cannot say that there is no contempt for the court except where they downgraded him twice, as is evident in [the chapter] Chezkas HaBatim (Bava Batra 32a). And one can answer that there is no contempt for the court except where they downgraded him on the basis of testimony, whereas in a downgrading that is on account of a rumor, there is no contempt for the court. And even though we say (Gittin 81a) regarding a divorced woman [marrying] a priest that we do not nullify a rumor — that is because there is a remedy [for the situation]; however, here, where if we do not elevate him he will be disqualified forever, we do nullify [the rumor]. Alternatively, regarding rabbinic terumah, they were lenient.

Tosafot on Ketubot 26b:2:1.hebrew: אנן אחתינן ליה אנן מסקינן ליה - פי' בקונטרס אע"ג דתרי ותרי נינהו, אוקי תרי להדי תרי ואוקי גברא אחזקתיה. וקשה לר"י, דבפרק האומר בקדושין (דף סו. ושם) קאמר גבי ינאי: "היכי דמי? אילימא דתרי אמרי אשתבאי ותרי אמרי לא אשתבאי, מאי חזית דסמכת אהני" — פירוש: אהני דאמרו לא אשתבאי — "סמוך אהני"! ואמאי קאמר "ויבוקש הדבר ולא נמצא"? והתם פי' בקונטרס, דלא אמרי' אוקי תרי בהדי תרי ואוקי גברא אחזקיה, דהא לא באו להעיד על אמו אלא על ינאי, ולו לא היה חזקת כשרות. ואין נראה לר"י, דחזקת האם מהניא גם לינאי, כדמשמע הכא. ואמרינן נמי לעיל בפ"ק (כתובות דף יג. ושם): "לדברי המכשיר בה מכשיר בבתה", ואפילו מאן דפסל בבתה היינו משום דמעלה עשו גבי זנות. וגם אין לומר כמו שתירץ ר"ת, דליכא למימר התם אוקמינן אחזקה לפי שכל הנשים היו בחזקת שבויות; דא"כ, היכי מייתי מינה ראיה על אשתו שזינתה בעד אחד, דשאני התם דכל הנשים בחזקת שבויות, אבל אשתו זינתה היא בחזקת היתר? ונראה לר"י, דתרי ותרי ספיקא דרבנן הוא, ומדרבנן החמירו דלא מוקמינן לה אחזקה, והכא בתרומה דרבנן הקילו. ובפרק בכל מערבין (עירובין דף לה.) גבי תרומה ונטמאה כו': "ספק — הרי זה חמר גמל, דברי ר"מ", ומוקי לה רבה ורב יוסף בשתי כתי עדים; הא דלא מוקמינן לה אחזקתה דלא נטמאת, אע"ג דתרומה בזמן הזה דרבנן, היינו משום דערובי תחומין דאורייתא לר"מ. אי נמי: שאני התם דאיכא ריעותא דהרי נטמאת לפניך, ולא אמרינן "השתא הוא דאיטמי", אע"ג דגבי מקוה אמרינן "השתא הוא דחסר ואתאי" (נדה דף ב:) — הכא דאיכא שתי כתי עדים, לא אמרינן "השתא הוא דאיטמי". וב"שנים אומרים מת ושנים אומרים לא מת" דאמרינן לעיל (כתובות דף כב:): "לא תצא", ולא מוקמינן לה אחזקת אשת איש — היינו משום דחזקה דאשה דייקא ומנסבא מרעה לה לחזקת אשת איש. אע"ג דבשנים אומרים מת אמרינן בהאשה רבה (יבמות פז:) דמותרת לחזור לו, וכיון דליכא חומרא בסוף לא דייקא — מ"מ הכא, כיון דמכחישין זה את זה, איכא חומרא. וב"שנים אומרים נתגרשה ושנים אומרים לא נתגרשה" דאמרינן נמי "לא תצא", אע"ג דלא דייקא וליכא נמי חזקה דאין האשה מעיזה פניה — דשלא בפני בעלה מעיזה, וכ"ש היכא דמסייעין לה עדים — ויש לומר דמכל מקום דייקא, לפי שיראה שיוזמו עדיה או יפסלו אותם בגזלנותא. ובהאשה רבה (שם צג: ושם) גבי "בעו מיניה מרב ששת: עד אחד ביבמה מהו" כו', "אמר להו: תניתוה, אמרו לה מת בנך ואחר כך מת בעליך ונתייבמה, ואח"כ אמרו לה חילוף הדברים — תצא, והולד ראשון והאחרון ממזר; היכי דמי? אילימא תרי ותרי, מאי חזית דסמכת אהני דאסרי ליבם? סמוך אהני דשרו לה!" וקשה: דמאי פריך? והא אית לן לאוקמי אחזקה דאסורה ליבם שמת בעלה תחלה, כדאמרינן בפרק ארבעה אחין (יבמות דף לא. ושם) גבי "נפל הבית עליו ועל בת אחיו" כו'! ועוד: כיון דתרי ותרי ספיקא דרבנן הוא, יש לאוסרה כדאמרינן גבי ינאי, והתם לא דייקא, כדאמרינן התם "זימנין דרחמא ליה ליבם"! וי"ל, דמ"מ מהני דיוקא דידה לענין דמרעה ליה לחזקת איסור ליבם. והא דפריך נמי התם כו', ועוד: "ממזר? ספק ממזר הוא!" — אע"ג דבחזקת איסור ליבם היא, מ"מ לא הוי ממזר ודאי, דמהני דיוקא דידה כדפרשינן; ועוד: כיון דתרי ותרי ספיקא דרבנן, אין לנו להעמידה על חזקתה ולהתירו בממזרת. ורבינו יצחק בר ברוך פי', דלא אמרינן בכל הני אוקמא אחזקה, לפי שהשנים שמוציאים אותו מחזקתו של היתר הם מעידים תחלה, ומיד כשהעידו יצא מחזקתו ע"י עדותן, ותו לא אמרינן אוקמא אחזקה. ולהכי פריך לעיל: מאי שנא רישא ומאי שנא סיפא? דשנים שאומרים נתקדשה העידו תחלה, ובשנים אומרים נתגרשה, אע"פ שהם העידו תחלה, מ"מ היתה בחזקת אשת איש. וכן ההיא דהאשה רבה ודינאי — שנים המוציאין אותו מחזקתו באו תחלה. ואין נראה לרבינו יצחק, דהא הכא בשמעתין מוקמינן ליה אחזקה, אע"ג דכבר פסלוהו השנים והוציאוהו מחזקתו, ואין סברא שיועיל מה שעד אחד המכשיר העיד קודם; ועוד, דרב אשי משמע דבעי למימר דאפילו אתו שניהם לבסוף, דמסקינן ליה:
Tosafot on Ketubot 26b:2:1.english: We downgrade him, we elevate him - Rashi explained [that] even though they are two [witnesses] against two, set two opposite two and establish the person in his [original] presumptive status. And [this] is difficult for Ri [Rabbeinu Yitzchak], for in the chapter HaOmer in Kiddushin (66a and there [in Tosafot]) [the Gemara] says regarding Yannai: "What are the circumstances? If we say that two say she was taken captive and two say she was not taken captive, what do you see to rely on these" — meaning, on those who say she was not taken captive — "rely on these [others]! And why does [the verse] state, 'And the matter was investigated and it was not found'?" And there, Rashi explained that we do not say "set two opposite two and establish the person in his presumptive status," because they did not come to testify about his mother, but rather about Yannai, and he did not have a presumptive status of fitness. But [this] does not seem [correct] to Ri, because the presumptive status of the mother is effective for Yannai as well, as is implied here. And we also say above in the first chapter (Ketubot 13a and there [in Tosafot]): "According to the one who declares her fit, he declares her daughter fit," and even the one who disqualifies her daughter — that is because they made a higher standard regarding promiscuity. And furthermore, one cannot say as Rabbeinu Tam resolved, that one cannot say there "we establish [her] in [her] presumptive status" because all women were in the presumptive status of being captives; for if so, how does [the Gemara] bring a proof from it regarding his wife who committed adultery [testified to] by one witness — [which would be refutable by saying] that there it is different because all women are in the presumptive status of being captives, whereas his wife who committed adultery is in a presumptive status of permissibility? Rather, it seems to Ri that two [witnesses] against two is a Rabbinic uncertainty, and by Rabbinic law they were stringent not to establish it in its presumptive status, whereas here, with terumah, which is Rabbinic, they were lenient. And in the chapter BeKol Me'arvin (Eruvin 35a) regarding "terumah and it became impure, etc.: [if it is] uncertain, he is [like] a donkey-driver and a camel-driver, the words of Rabbi Meir," which Rabbah and Rav Yosef establish as [a case of] two pairs of witnesses — the reason we do not establish it in its presumptive status of not having become impure, even though terumah nowadays is Rabbinic, is because eruvei techumin is Biblical according to Rabbi Meir. Alternatively: there it is different because there is a flaw [in the presumptive status], for behold it became impure before you, and we do not say "it just now became impure"; even though regarding a mikveh we say "it just now became lacking and [became deficient]" (Niddah 2b) — here, where there are two pairs of witnesses, we do not say "it just now became impure." And regarding [the case of] "two say he died and two say he did not die," where we say above (Ketubot 22b) "she shall not leave [her second husband]" and we do not establish her in the presumptive status of a married woman — that is because the presumption that a woman investigates carefully and [only then] marries weakens the presumptive status of a married woman. Even though regarding "two say he died" we say in [the chapter] HaIshah Rabbah (Yevamot 87b) that she is permitted to return to him, and since there is no stringency at the end she does not investigate carefully — nevertheless here, since they contradict each other, there is a stringency. And regarding "two say she was divorced and two say she was not divorced," where we also say "she shall not leave" even though she does not investigate carefully and there is also no presumption that a woman is not brazen [in front of her husband], because outside the presence of her husband she is brazen, and all the more so where witnesses support her — one can say that nevertheless she investigates carefully, because she fears that her witnesses will be proven to be conspiring witnesses or will be disqualified as robbers. And in HaIshah Rabbah (ibid. 93b and there [in Tosafot]) regarding "they asked Rav Sheshet: what is [the law of] one witness regarding a yevamah, etc.? He said to them: You have learned it [in a Mishnah]: '[If] they told her: your son died and afterward your husband died, and she underwent yibbum, and afterward they told her the opposite — she must leave, and the first and last child are mamzerim.' What are the circumstances? If we say two against two, what do you see to rely on those who forbid [her] to the yavam? Rely on those who permit her!" And [this] is difficult: why does [the Gemara] ask [this]? Surely we ought to establish [her] in the presumptive status of being forbidden to the yavam because her husband died first, as we say in the chapter Arba'ah Achim (Yevamot 31a and there [in Tosafot]) regarding "the house collapsed upon him and upon his brother's daughter, etc."! And furthermore: since two against two is a Rabbinic uncertainty, we should forbid her, as we say regarding Yannai, and there she does not investigate carefully, as we say there, "sometimes she loves the yavam!" And one can answer that nevertheless her careful investigation is effective to the extent that it weakens the presumptive status of prohibition to the yavam. And as for what [the Gemara] also asks there, etc., and furthermore: "[Is he] a mamzer? He is a doubtful mamzer!" — even though she is in the presumptive status of prohibition to the yavam, nevertheless he is not a definite mamzer, because her careful investigation is effective as we explained; and furthermore, since two against two is a Rabbinic uncertainty, we should not establish her in her presumptive status and permit him [to marry] a mamzeret. And Rabbeinu Yitzchak bar Baruch explained that we do not say in all these [cases] "establish it in its presumptive status," because the two [witnesses] who remove him from his presumptive status of permissibility testified first, and immediately when they testified he left his presumptive status through their testimony, and we no longer say "establish it in its presumptive status." And therefore [the Gemara] asks above: what is different [in] the first clause and what is different [in] the latter clause? Because the two who say she was betrothed testified first, whereas in [the case of] "two say she was divorced," even though they testified first, nevertheless she was in the presumptive status of a married woman. And similarly [in] that [case] of HaIshah Rabbah and of Yannai — the two who remove him from his presumptive status came first. But [this] does not seem [correct] to Rabbeinu Yitzchak, for behold here in our sugya we establish him in his presumptive status even though the two [witnesses] already disqualified him and removed him from his presumptive status, and there is no logic that it should help that the one witness who declares him fit testified first; and furthermore, from Rav Ashi it is implied that he wishes to say that even if both of them came at the end, we elevate him.

Tosafot on Ketubot 26b:6:1.hebrew: על ידי ממון מותרת לבעלה - נראה דמותרת אפילו לבעלה כהן, דלא חיישינן אפי' לאונסא, משום דמרתתי להפסיד ממונם, ולא דמי לשבויה. וכן מוכח בגמרא, דקאמר: "לא שנו אלא שיד ישראל תקיפה על העובדי כוכבים, אבל יד העובדי כוכבים תקיפה על עצמן — אפילו ע"י ממון אסורה לבעלה", ועל כרחן היינו לכהונה, מדקאמרי "אף אנן נמי תנינא" מההיא ד"ריחקוה בני משפחתה", והא לא שייך אלא לכהונה, דבישראל לא שייך "וריחקוה בני משפחתה", דאינה אסורה אלא לבעלה. ועוד ראיה, דתנן בפ' שני דמסכת ע"ז (דף כב.): "אין מעמידין בהמה בפונדקאות של עובדי כוכבים מפני שחשודים על הרביעה", ורמינהו: "לוקחין מהן בהמה לקרבן", "לא קשיא, הא לכתחלה והא דיעבד; ומנא תימרא דשני בין לכתחלה כו', דתנן: לא תתייחד אשה עמהם מפני שחשודים על העריות, ורמינהו: האשה שנחבשה ע"י עובדי כוכבים ע"י ממון מותרת לבעלה, אלא ש"מ שני לן בין לכתחלה לדיעבד". משמע דאין לחוש כלל שנבעלה, דאי "מותרת לבעלה" ישראל קאמר, דלא חיישינן שמא נתרצת, אבל לבעלה כהן אסורה דחיישינן שמא נאנסה — א"כ לא הוה מייתי מידי:
Tosafot on Ketubot 26b:6:1.english: Due to a monetary [matter], she is permitted to her husband - It appears that she is permitted even to her husband [who is] a priest, for we are not concerned even about forced [relations], because they are afraid of losing their money, and it is not comparable to a captive [woman]. And so it is proven in the Gemara, where it says: "They taught this only when the hand of Israel is dominant over the gentiles, but when the hand of the gentiles is dominant over themselves, even due to a monetary [matter] she is forbidden to her husband" — and perforce this refers to the priesthood, since they say, "We too have learned [this in a Mishnah]," from that [case] of "her family members distanced her," and that applies only to the priesthood; for regarding a [non-priest] Israelite, "and her family members distanced her" does not apply, since she is forbidden only to her husband. And [there is] another proof, as we learned in a Mishnah in the second chapter of Tractate Avodah Zarah (22a): "One may not place an animal in inns of gentiles because they are suspected of bestiality." And [the Gemara] raises a contradiction: "One may buy an animal from them for a sacrifice." [The Gemara answers:] "There is no difficulty: this [refers to] ab initio and that [refers to] ex post facto. And from where do you say that we distinguish between ab initio etc.? As we learned in a Mishnah: A woman may not be secluded with them because they are suspected of forbidden sexual relations. And [the Gemara] raises a contradiction: 'A woman who was imprisoned by gentiles due to a monetary [matter] is permitted to her husband.' Rather, learn from this that we distinguish between ab initio and ex post facto." This implies that there is no concern at all that she had sexual relations; for if it meant "she is permitted to her Israelite husband," because we are not concerned lest she consented, but to her priestly husband she is forbidden because we are concerned lest she was forced — if so, [the Gemara] would not have brought any [proof].

Tosafot on Ketubot 26b:6:2.hebrew: ועל ידי נפשות אסורה לבעלה - היינו אפילו לבעלה ישראל, דחיישינן שמא נתרצת כדי למצא חן שלא יהרגנה; דאי לבעלה כהן קאמר, ואסורה שמא נאנסה, א"כ הוה ליה למימר "אסורה לכהונה", אלא ודאי אפילו לבעלה ישראל אסורה. וא"ת: צנועות לישתרו, דקודם לכן מסרן נפשייהו, כדמשמע בריש מכילתין (דף ג:) גבי "כל הנשאת ברביעי תיבעל להשר תחלה"? וצריך לומר: דהכא חיישינן על כל אחת שמא אינה צנועה, ואפילו נראית צנועה שמא אינה:
Tosafot on Ketubot 26b:6:2.english: "And due to a capital [offense], she is forbidden to her husband" - That is, even to her Israelite husband, for we are concerned that perhaps she consented [to relations] in order to find favor [with her captor] so that he would not kill her; for if [the Mishnah] were speaking of her priestly husband, and she is forbidden [because] perhaps she was coerced, if so, it should have stated, "she is forbidden to the priesthood"; rather, [it] certainly [means that] she is forbidden even to her Israelite husband. And if you will say: Modest women should be permitted, since previously they would give up their lives [rather than submit], as is implied at the beginning of our tractate (3b) regarding [the decree that] "whoever marries on Wednesday shall have relations with the governor first"? One must say: Here we are concerned regarding each [woman] that perhaps she is not modest, and even [one who] appears modest, perhaps she is not [modest].
